corn.description: It grows on a tall plant and has yellow kernels.

bugs.description: They are small and crawl on six legs.

nuts.description: They have a hard shell and fall from trees.

crab.description: It walks sideways and has big claws.

clams.description: They live in a shell that opens and shuts.

worms.description: They wiggle in the dirt after rain.

grapes.description: They grow in bunches on a vine.

apples.description: They are crunchy fruits that grow on trees.

shrimp.description: It has a curled body and long feelers.

lizards.description: They are small reptiles with four legs and a long tail.

geckos.description: They are little lizards with sticky toes.

tadpoles.description: They are baby frogs that swim with their tails.

crickets.description: They are insects that chirp at night.

mice.description: They are tiny animals with long tails and round ears.

leaves.description: They grow on trees and turn colors in fall.

clover.description: It is a small plant with three round leaves.

acorns.description: They are nuts that grow on oak trees.

berries.description: They are small, sweet fruits that grow on bushes.

rats.description: They look like big mice with long tails.

gerbils.description: They are small, sandy brown animals that dig.

facts: Raccoons have black fur around their eyes. It looks like a mask!

care_notes.good: A rough branch to rub on

facts: A green vine snake is long and thin, just like a vine.
Its bright green color helps it hide in the leaves.
It has a long, pointy nose.
It likes to eat lizards and frogs.

facts: A baby deer is called a fawn.

Male deer grow antlers and lose them every year.
Deer can run fast and jump very high.

facts: A baby bear is called a cub.
Bears sleep through much of the winter in a den.
Black bears are great tree climbers.
Bears have a super strong sense of smell.

care_notes.text: The owl is quiet and watchful.

facts: Owls can turn their heads very far around.
Most owls hunt at night.
Owls fly almost without a sound.
A baby owl is called an owlet.
